article_title: containerd Patches Four Moderate Advisories on October 13 Across 2.4, 2.3, 2.2 and 2.0, With 2.0.14 Carrying Only a Disk-Exhaustion Fix

content_preview.title: containerd Patches Four Moderate Advisories on October 13 Across 2.4, 2.3, 2.2 and 2.0, With 2.0.14 Carrying Only a Disk-Exhaustion Fix
content_preview.summary: containerd 2.4.2, 2.3.7, 2.2.10 and 2.0.14 shipped October 13 with fixes for four Moderate-rated advisories, split unevenly by branch; 2.0.14 lists one.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The containerd project published four patch releases on October 13, 2026: [2.4.2](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.2), [2.3.7](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.7), [2.2.10](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.10) and [2.0.14](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.0.14). Each release page describes itself as containing security patches or a security patch. Across the four, the release notes ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Dense but well organised News piece: Overview, per-advisory section, per-release matrix, hardening items kept separate, workarounds, What We Don't Know. 811 words by raw count and 811 with link URLs stripped, within News 400-1200. Title is 135 characters (cap 150). No policy violation.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 9 snapshots (source-0..8.html.gz) after gunzip + tag-stripping; all 9 have status 200, null error, no archive_fallback, and contain the page body (not page chrome only): the 4 release pages carry the full release notes (Security Updates, Highlights, Contributors), the 4 advisory pages carry Impact/Patches/Workarounds/Credits/Severity/CVE/Weaknesses, the index page lists 10 advisories. manifest suspicious_patterns: none for any source. Per-advisory verification (snapshot, cross-checked against the GitHub REST API repos/containerd/containerd/security-advisories): GHSA-vwhp-8p66-mq4f: Moderate (API: medium), CVE ID CVE-2026-95839, 'No CWEs', no CVSS shown, affected >= 2.2.0 < 2.2.10, >= 2.3.0 < 2.3.7, >= 2.4.0 < 2.4.2, patched 2.2.10, 2.3.7, 2.4.2; unrecovered panic on io.containerd.manifest.subject annotation with malformed digest; published Oct 13, 2026 (22:52:05Z); credits melihgurlek, ssst0n3, zj1ng7, OpenSec Intelligence; workaround: restrict image references to trusted registries. Matches the article. GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc: Moderate, No known CVE, CWE-20/400/770, no CVSS, same ranges and patched versions as above (2.2.10, 2.3.7, 2.4.2); affects only configs with concurrent_layer_fetch_buffer set, default (0) not affected, running containers unaffected; workaround keep it at 0/omitted plus trusted registries; published 22:53:58Z; finder Kushalkhemka. Matches. GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66: Moderate, No known CVE, CWE-400, no CVSS, affected >= 2.0.0 < 2.0.14 plus the 2.2, 2.3, 2.4 ranges, patched 2.4.2, 2.3.7, 2.2.10, 2.0.14; disk exhaustion from unbounded layer stream, node disk pressure / kubelet unresponsive / blocked pod startup as stated; published 22:50:43Z (article's '22:50 UTC' is correct); reporter Jakub Ciolek of AlphaSense. Matches. It is the only advisory whose range includes 2.0.x. GHSA-5p7c-hggf-c748: Moderate, No known CVE, CWE-400/772, no CVSS, affected >= 2.2.0 < 2.2.10 and >= 2.3.0 < 2.3.7, patched 2.2.10, 2.3.7 only; 2.4 stated not vulnerable (no restore via CRI); enable_criu=false or enable_experimental_restore_via_create=false (default from 2.3.4 and 2.2.7); /tmp/checkpoint* unmount or reboot; published 22:48:30Z; reporter IamwhatIamSY. Matches. No advisory page or API record shows a CVSS vector/score; the article makes no CVSS claim, so nothing to correct. No advisory mentions 1.x; the article's 'What We Don't Know' states the sources do not address other lines. Release notes (snapshots and API release bodies): v2.4.2 Security Updates = CVE-2026-95839, GHSA-8647, GHSA-hc94 (3); v2.3.7 = CVE-2026-95839, GHSA-5p7c, GHSA-8647, GHSA-hc94 (4); v2.2.10 = same 4; v2.0.14 = GHSA-hc94 only (1). Each matches the 'patched versions' lines of the four advisories, so the title claim '2.0.14 Carrying Only a Disk-Exhaustion Fix' holds (hc94 is the disk-exhaustion advisory). CVE-to-advisory link: not merely the writer's inference from matching IDs - in the release notes the CVE-2026-95839 entry is a hyperlink whose href is .../advisories/GHSA-vwhp-8p66-mq4f (checked in source-0 HTML and the API body), and the GHSA-vwhp page itself shows CVE ID CVE-2026-95839. The article words it as 'appears on the page of a fourth advisory' and '(the CVE belongs to GHSA-vwhp-8p66-mq4f)', both supported. Hardening items verified per release: symlink log-file hardening and seccomp socket allow-list in all four; '..' path rejection in 2.4.2/2.3.7/2.2.10 only; ID-mapping label filtering in 2.3.7/2.2.10/2.0.14 only (not 2.4.2); 2.4.2 excessive-memory-during-pulls fix; 2.2.10 hang/data-corruption multipart fetch fix. The article keeps these separate from advisories and says the notes do not tie them together. Dates via API: releases published 2.0.14 22:26:41Z, 2.4.2 22:35:06Z, 2.2.10 22:45:01Z, 2.3.7 22:46:58Z (snapshots show 22:26, 22:35, 22:45, 22:46); advisories published 22:48-22:53Z on Oct 13; all dates are Oct 13 UTC as stated. Advisory index: snapshot lists 10 advisories, 3 dated Oct 13 (8647, vwhp, 5p7c), hc94 absent - exactly as the article reports. Re-checked live (curl of /security/advisories on review day, 2026-10-14): the HTML index still lists the same 10 IDs and still omits GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66, although the REST API returns it as published (2026-10-13T22:50:43Z, severity medium). The article's statement stays accurate; no change since the snapshot. Live re-fetch of release bodies and advisory metadata through the API showed no change from the snapshots. Internal links: none (all links are github.com sources, all 9 in article.sources, no orphans). Allowlist: github.com already present as an exact line; no change needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every GHSA ID, CVE, severity label (Moderate for all four), affected/patched ranges, release contents, workarounds and counts (4 releases, 4 advisories; 2.4.2 -> 3, 2.3.7 -> 4, 2.2.10 -> 4, 2.0.14 -> 1) trace to snapshots and were re-verified against the GitHub API. Vendor claims are attributed to the advisory pages. No cross-advisory generalisation: 5p7c is correctly excluded from 2.4.2 and 2.0.14, and 8647/vwhp are correctly excluded from 2.0.14. The article gives no CWE, CVSS or reporter credits and claims none.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributed, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. Freshness: reported as published October 13, 2026 with no exploitation claims; 'What We Don't Know' states exploitation status is unaddressed.
editor_notes.originality: No prior containerd coverage in the archive (grep of 2026-09 and 2026-10 articles returned none). New topic.
concerns: The HTML advisory index (snapshot and live re-check) omits GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66 while the advisory page and REST API show it published; the article reports this without speculating on the cause.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE. Accurate, per-advisory verified, correctly scoped title, all 9 sources read and cross-checked via the GitHub API, no prompt-injection patterns, no allowlist changes needed.
